 'status': 'complete',
 'statement': 'Let T(A) be the finite, nonempty ordered binary trees with leaves labelled in A, generated by leaf(a) and node(L,R). A model M consists of a real number u >= 0 and a function r: R -> R such that for every z in R there exists a real delta with |delta| <= u and r(z) = z(1+delta). Write mul_M(a,b)=r(ab) and add_M(a,b)=r(a+b). Tree.map applies its function to each leaf and preserves every node. Define depth(leaf(a))=0 and depth(node(L,R))=1+max(depth(L),depth(R)). For a real-labelled tree S, exactSum(leaf(x))=x and exactSum(node(L,R))=exactSum(L)+exactSum(R). Define roundedSum_M(leaf(x))=x and roundedSum_M(node(L,R))=r(roundedSum_M(L)+roundedSum_M(R)). For any real bound b, IsPerturbation(b,S,Sprime) means that S and Sprime have the same ordered tree shape and that every corresponding pair of real leaf values x,y satisfies |y-x| <= b|x|; it is generated precisely by this leaf condition and the componentwise node rule. For k in N and v in R, gamma(k,v)=(kv)/(1-kv), with k cast to R. The constructions replace each pair-valued leaf (a,b) by either ab or r(ab), preserving the tree, and then the dot-product construction combines the latter leaves using r after each internal addition. For every model and every input tree t in T(R x R), if (depth(t)+1)u < 1, the constructed rounded dot product equals the exact sum of some real-labelled tree that perturbs the exact product leaves by at most gamma(depth(t)+1,u) in relative absolute error. The other targets specify the leafwise rounded-product construction, its u-relative perturbation property, and the equality mul_M(a,b)=r(ab).',
 'targets': [
  {'name': 'Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedDotProduct_exists_perturbation', 'statement': 'For every model M (with u=u(M) and r=round(M) satisfying the model conditions) and every finite nonempty ordered binary tree t with leaf labels in R x R, let d=depth(t). If (d+1)u < 1, then there exists a tree P in T(R) such that IsPerturbation(gamma(d+1,u), exactProductTree(t), P) and exactSum(P)=roundedDotProduct(M,t). Explicitly, P has exactly the shape of t, each leaf (a,b) of t corresponds to a real leaf p of P with |p-ab| <= ((d+1)u/(1-(d+1)u))|ab|, and the ordinary sum of all these p equals the result of rounding each product ab with r and recursively rounding each internal addition with r. The natural number d+1 is cast to R in the inequality and quotient. The smallness hypothesis makes the denominator strictly positive. No balance or sign restriction is imposed on t or its real labels.'},
  {'name': 'Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedProductTerm.eq_1', 'statement': 'For every model M and all real numbers x,y, roundedProductTerm(M,x,y)=mul_M(x,y). By the supplied definition of mul_M, this value is r(xy), where r=round(M). Thus the leaf transformation used by roundedProductTree is the model rounding of the exact real product. There is no additional hypothesis.'},
  {'name': 'Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedProductTree.eq_1', 'statement': 'For every model M and every t in T(R x R), roundedProductTree(M,t)=Tree.map((a,b) -> roundedProductTerm(M,a,b),t). This equality specifies that every pair-valued leaf is replaced by r(ab) and all internal nodes are preserved; it performs no additions or products between subtrees. There is no additional hypothesis.'},
  {'name': 'Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedProductTree_isPerturbation', 'statement': 'For every model M and every t in T(R x R), IsPerturbation(u(M),exactProductTree(t),roundedProductTree(M,t)). Equivalently, these two constructed trees have the same ordered shape and, at every corresponding input leaf (a,b), |r(ab)-ab| <= u(M)|ab|. This is a bound on the leaf products before the rounded additions in roundedDotProduct. There is no depth or smallness hypothesis.'},
  {'name': 'Research.FloatingPoint.Model.mul.eq_1', 'statement': 'For every model M and all real numbers a,b, mul_M(a,b)=round(M)(ab), with ab the exact real product. This specifies the operation used by roundedProductTerm and hence by every leaf of roundedProductTree. There is no additional hypothesis.'}
 ],
 'constructions': [
  {'name': 'Research.BinaryTreeReduction.exactProductTree', 'description': 'A function T(R x R) -> T(R). For every input tree t, exactProductTree(t)=Tree.map((a,b) -> ab,t): a leaf (a,b) becomes the single real leaf ab, and a node becomes a node of the recursively transformed children. It preserves tree shape and does not multiply subtree values together. Its output supplies the reference leaf values for both perturbation theorems.'},
  {'name': 'Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedDotProduct', 'description': 'A function taking any model M and any t in T(R x R) to a real number: roundedDotProduct(M,t)=roundedSum(M,roundedProductTree(M,t)). Equivalently, its value at leaf(a,b) is r(ab); its value at node(L,R) is r(roundedDotProduct(M,L)+roundedDotProduct(M,R)). Thus there is one application of r to each exact leaf product and one application of r to each internal sum. The tree determines the grouping of additions. The existence target represents precisely this computed real value as exactSum(P) for a leafwise perturbation P of exactProductTree(t), under the stated depth-dependent smallness condition.'},
  {'name': 'Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedProductTree', 'description': 'A function taking any model M and any t in T(R x R) to a tree in T(R): roundedProductTree(M,t)=Tree.map((a,b) -> roundedProductTerm(M,a,b),t), where roundedProductTerm(M,a,b)=mul_M(a,b)=r(ab). It replaces each leaf independently, preserves every internal node, and performs no aggregation at those nodes. Its defining equality is one target, and another target states that it is a u(M)-relative leafwise perturbation of exactProductTree(t). It is the intermediate tree passed to roundedSum in roundedDotProduct.'}
 ],
 'assumptions': [
  'Every occurrence of a model quantifies over the supplied Model type: u is real with 0 <= u, r maps all real numbers to real numbers, and for every real z there exists a real delta (allowed to depend on z) with |delta| <= u and r(z)=z(1+delta). These are part of the model data, not extra hypotheses inferred from the name floating point.',
  'Every input tree is an arbitrary finite nonempty ordered binary tree with real-pair leaf labels. All leaf coordinates and arithmetic results have domain R. The existential perturbed tree in the main target has real leaf labels. No balanced-tree, nonzero-input, positivity-of-input, or representability condition is supplied.',
  'Only roundedDotProduct_exists_perturbation requires the additional inequality (depth(t)+1)u(M) < 1. The other four targets are universally quantified without additional premises beyond membership in their stated domains and the model conditions.',
  'The perturbation bound is relative to each exact product ab, not separately to a and b. If ab=0, the leaf inequality forces the corresponding perturbed value to be 0. The main theorem asserts existence of perturbed real product values, without specifying perturbed pairs of input factors.'
 ],
 'missing_context': []
}
assert [x['name'] for x in result['targets']] == data['targets']
assert [x['name'] for x in result['constructions']] == data['construction_names']
os.makedirs('/output', exist_ok=True)
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix='.translation-', suffix='.json', dir='/output')
try:
    with os.fdopen(fd,'w') as f:
        json.dump(result,f,ensure_ascii=False,indent=2)
        f.write('\\n')
        f.flush()
        os.fsync(f.fileno())
    os.replace(path,'/output/translation.json')
finally:
    if os.path.exists(path): os.unlink(path)
print('Saved /output/translation.json; all 5 targets and 3 constructions included exactly once; status=complete.')
PY"
